name: Darn a sock
blurb: Twenty minutes of weaving saves a good pair of wool socks. A proper darn is a woven patch, not a pulled-together hole — and it lasts.
gear: A darning mushroom, a tennis ball or a light bulb
Darning yarn or fine wool in a matching weight
steps: Stretch the sock over the mushroom so the hole lies flat and open.
Run a circle of small running stitches around the hole in sound fabric to stop it spreading.
Lay parallel warp threads across the hole, anchoring well into the good fabric either side.
Weave the weft threads over and under the warp, packing each row snug against the last.
Keep the tension even and the patch flat — a tight darn creates a lump that causes blisters.
Finish by weaving the ends into the surrounding fabric rather than knotting.
tips: Pulling the hole closed instead of weaving across it makes a ridge you will feel with every step.
Darn while the hole is small — a thin patch is far easier than a large hole.
proof: A darned sock you can wear all day without noticing the repair.
